Applied to the bucket of everything closing today, it also fires on a leg that opens today — which is removed from an open set it was never in, then added by the entry step, and so never closes at all. It stays open to the end of the axis and indexes marks it does not have.
- ⚠ **The `IndexError` was luck.** The leg holds zero units until its entry runs, so its P&L is unaffected; had the mark array been long enough — which it is for any leg whose instrument keeps trading — the defect would have been a position silently held forever, contributing to exposure, concurrency and the equal-weight denominator on every subsequent date.
- Prevention: when a spec states an ordering rule over a set, ask **which members of the set the rule was written about**, and split the set on that predicate rather than applying it wholesale. Here: `closed_today = [leg for leg in closing[day] if entry_index[leg] < day]`, with the same-bar legs closed AFTER their own entry. A `bars_held = 0` test is the discriminator and it is not optional — the spec explicitly records that population as real.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `app/services/equity_curve.py::build_equity_curve` (the split, with rule 4's scope stated on it); `tests/test_equity_curve.py::TestSingleLegConservation::test_a_same_bar_leg_is_legal`; `scripts/probe_2240_statistics.py` probes 2 and 3 (the inversion injected both ways).

### A single-pass rebalance to `equity / n` leaves cash at MINUS the cost it just charged — that is leverage (#2240 5d, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: rebalancing every open position to `equity / n` and charging the half-spread on each traded delta ends the pass with `cash = -(total cost)`. The arithmetic is exact: targets sum to `equity`, so cash lands at zero, and the costs come out of a zero balance.
- Root cause: the target was computed on PRE-cost equity, so the pass promises to invest money it is about to spend on the trade. Netting the estimate back out does not close it either — trimming the target by the first-pass cost makes the sellers' deltas LARGER, so the second pass can cost more than the first and the residual flips negative again.
- ⚠ **The magnitude is ~0.5% of one rebalance and it is still not tolerable.** The project posture is no leverage, and a tolerance-based check ("cash >= -1e-6") is a decision to permit a small amount of it, which then has to be re-argued every time the cost model widens. It also compounds: 16,236 dates of a slightly-negative cash balance is a slowly-borrowing sleeve.
- Prevention: **model the rebalance the way a broker executes it — sells first, then buys capped by cash on hand.** `cash >= 0` then holds by construction rather than by tolerance, and the residual under-investment is exactly the cost charged, which is the honest answer. Assert it on the full population as `min(equity - invested) >= 0`, not on a fixture.
- ⚠ Same file, same shape, opposite direction: sizing a date's entries ONE AT A TIME gives the first entry 100% of a flat pot and reports every sibling as capital-constrained. Both entries are decided at the same instant on the same bar, so the denominator must count the whole basket — otherwise criterion 9's census carries a narrowing that never happened, and a narrowing that did not happen is as misleading as one that is not counted.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `app/services/equity_curve.py::SIZING_RULE_ID` note 3 and `build_equity_curve`'s rebalance block; `tests/test_equity_curve.py::TestRebalance::test_cash_never_goes_negative_which_is_what_sells_before_buys_buys` and `::test_entries_on_the_SAME_date_are_sized_against_the_whole_basket`; `scripts/verify_2240_statistics.py` property P2; `scripts/probe_2240_statistics.py` probes 4 and 8.

### `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` does not bind a superuser — measure the connection's role BEFORE designing any database-level access control (#2240 5e-1, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: acceptance C5 requires the backtest hold-out to be *"mechanically inaccessible to exploratory queries — logging alone is not the criterion, which says governance fails"*. The textbook Postgres answer is row-level security, and `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE` plus `… FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` is documented as binding the table OWNER, which is what makes it look sufficient for a single-role application.
- Root cause: it does not bind a SUPERUSER, and it does not bind a role with `BYPASSRLS`. Measured on this database rather than reasoned: a two-row table with `ENABLE` + `FORCE` and a `USING (ns = 'in_sample')` policy returned **2 of 2 rows**, because `select current_user, rolsuper, rolbypassrls from pg_roles where rolname = current_user` is `('postgres', true, true)` — every connection this app opens uses `settings.database_url`, and that URL's role is `postgres`.
- ⚠ **A policy that the only caller walks through is worse than no policy.** It is #2288's *"a label nobody gates on is worse than no label: it looks like control and provides none"*, one layer down — and worse here, because RLS in `pg_policies` reads to a later maintainer as an enforced boundary.
- Prevention: **before shipping RLS, a `SECURITY DEFINER` wrapper, a `REVOKE`, or any other role-scoped control, run the two-line probe against the real connection and paste the result into the migration header.** Where the role turns out to be privileged, pick a mechanism that has no bypass bit: a **VIEW** filters for every role including a superuser, and a **TRIGGER** fires for every role including a superuser. Both were measured this run — the view's `WITH CASCADED CHECK OPTION` refused with SQLSTATE `44000`, the trigger with `23000`.
- ⚠ Corollary on naming: when the mechanism is a view, put the FILTERED relation behind the OBVIOUS name and the storage behind one you have to decide to type (`strategy_results` is the view, `strategy_results_store` is the table). The failure mode is not a determined adversary — it is withheld rows arriving in a result set nobody asked for.
- ⚠ **When you then VERIFY such a mechanism, assert the SQLSTATE, not the exception class.** `psycopg.errors.IntegrityError` covers 23000 (the trigger's `integrity_constraint_violation`), 23505 (unique), 23502 (not null) and 23503 (foreign key) alike — so a verifier catching it bare reports "the trigger refused" for a refusal the trigger never made. Measured this run: a duplicate probe row raises `UniqueViolation` / **23505**, which a bare catch swallows and an sqlstate assertion flags. The exception class is only a sufficient assertion where it is unique to the mechanism (`WithCheckOptionViolation` is; `IntegrityError` is not). Raised as a review WARNING on PR #2367.
- Caught by: running the probe instead of citing the documentation, at the point the mechanism was being chosen rather than after it shipped.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `sql/264_strategy_holdout_namespace.sql`'s header (the probe and its output, inline); `tests/test_strategy_holdout_namespace.py::test_row_level_security_would_not_have_bound_this_connection`, which re-runs the measurement and FAILS if a non-superuser role ever appears — the signal to revisit the decision; `scripts/verify_2240_holdout_namespace.py --mechanism`.

### A `SELECT *` view freezes its column list at CREATE time — a later `ADD COLUMN` on the base table is invisible, silently (#2240 5e-1, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT * FROM t` reads as "v is t", and it is not. Postgres expands the `*` once, at creation, and stores the resulting column list. `ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN x` adds nothing to `v`, and no error, warning or migration failure says so — every read through `v` simply lacks `x`.
- Root cause: the shorthand's meaning is "the columns that exist right now", but the code reads as "whatever the table has". This repo is exactly the shape where it bites: `sql/262` created `strategy_results` and `sql/263` added sixteen metric columns to it one stage later, so the ADD-COLUMN-after-the-fact pattern is the established one, not the exception.
- ⚠ **Naming the columns explicitly does NOT fix it** — an explicit list has the same staleness with the same silence. The only thing that fixes it is a check that the two lists are equal.
- Prevention: **pair every `SELECT *` view over a table that is still growing with a column-parity test** against `information_schema.columns`, and state in the migration header that a later ADD COLUMN must re-run `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`. The test is five lines and it converts a silent omission into a named failure.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `sql/264_strategy_holdout_namespace.sql` (the warning sits on the `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`); `tests/test_strategy_holdout_namespace.py::test_the_view_exposes_every_stored_column`; `scripts/verify_2240_holdout_namespace.py --mechanism` (prints both counts every run).

### Adding a TRIGGER to a table under test turns every `pytest.raises(Error)` case into a test of the trigger — and they all still pass (#2240 5e-1, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: `tests/test_strategy_results_table.py` has ~35 parametrised negative cases, each asserting that one malformed field is refused by the constraint that names it, all built from a shared `_BASE` row whose `namespace` was `hold_out`. Stage 5e-1 added a trigger refusing any `hold_out` row with no access record. **Every one of those 35 cases would still have passed** — refused by the new trigger, on the first statement, before the constraint under test was ever reached.
- Root cause: the assertion is `pytest.raises(psycopg.errors.Error)`, which is satisfied by ANY refusal. A shared fixture row is a shared premise, and a new blanket refusal on that row invalidates every test built from it at once while leaving the suite green. The tighter the exception class the smaller the hole, but `IntegrityError` would not have helped here either — the trigger raises `integrity_constraint_violation` deliberately.
- ⚠ **The direction matters: it is silent in the safe-looking direction.** A test that starts failing gets investigated; a test that keeps passing for a new reason gets nothing. There is no run in which this announces itself.
- Prevention: **when you add a table-wide refusal (trigger, new NOT NULL, new CHECK over the whole row), grep for every test fixture that constructs a row of that table and check whether the fixture's base row now trips it.** If it does, move the fixture off the tripping value — do not add the satisfying precondition to the fixture, because that makes the new refusal a silent precondition of 35 unrelated tests. Here `_BASE["namespace"]` moved to `in_sample` and the hold-out path got its own file.
- ⚠ Same test-quality shape as the phase-5d probe finding *"a test named after a branch that cannot fire is a test that passes for the wrong reason"* — both are tests that are green while asserting something other than what their name claims.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `tests/test_strategy_results_table.py::_BASE` (the comment states both reasons and points at the file that owns the hold-out path); `tests/test_strategy_holdout_namespace.py`.
## A parser whose line structure comes from SOURCE newlines is reading the filer's formatting, not the document (#2358, 2026-08-07)

- First seen in: #2358, filed off #2169's Codex checkpoint-2 pass, then measured.
  `_strip_inline_html` replaced EVERY tag with a space, `<br>` included. Interior
  newlines survived only because `_INLINE_WHITESPACE_RE` is `[ \t\r\f\v]+` and does not
  include `\n` — so the "lines" of a table cell were whichever newlines the filer
  agent happened to emit into the source, not the line breaks the markup specifies.
  Two filers rendering the identical Item 403 row parsed differently.
- Symptom: it does not surface as a dropped row, which is the tell. `<br>` → space →
  `'486,340 658,400'`, and `_parse_share_count` strips spaces AND commas, so the cell
  parses to **486,340,658,400** and is STORED. Full population of
  `def14a_beneficial_holdings` on 2026-08-07: 30 rows above 1e10 across 9 accessions,
  worst `3,183,454,219,115,736`. The name side collapses the same way — `Karen
  David-Green George Damiris Rodney Eads` is three people in one holder identity — so
  one defect costs a wrong amount AND a wrong holder count. Every other gate is
  silent: the row exists, the table scores, the job reports success.
- Prevention: (1) when a parser segments text extracted from HTML, the segmentation
  must come from BLOCK-LEVEL MARKUP (`<br>`, `<p>`, `<div>`, `<li>`), never from
  source newlines — those are formatting and vary by filer agent; (2) the fix belongs
  on a PARALLEL grid, not in the shared cell extractor. `_strip_inline_html` feeds
  `_score_table_headers` and `_resolve_columns`, which substring-match SEC-prescribed
  multi-word captions on `" ".join(headers).lower()` — `Amount<br/>and Nature
  of<br/>Beneficial Ownership` stops matching `"amount and nature"` the moment the tag
  becomes a newline, and table selection moves corpus-wide. That is the #2164 incident
  and the `expand_spans=False` pin of #2350, third occurrence. `_RawTable.line_rows`
  carries the line-structured grid, `rows` stays byte-identical, and the Item 403
  holder split is its only reader — a structural pin rather than a flag a future
  caller can forget.
- ⚠ **Mark tag-derived breaks with a SENTINEL, not with `\n`.** Once both are `\n` you
  cannot tell "the markup asked for a break" from "the filer wrapped the source", and
  every collapse rule you write is wrong for one of them. Four shapes all had to
  survive and they are only separable before the sentinel is resolved: `</p>\n<p>`
  (adjacent boundaries, ONE break), `<p>&nbsp;</p>` **and `<p><br/></p>`** (an empty
  block — a real BLANK line, which is the separator #2169's holder split reads), a run
  of consecutive `<br>`s (also a blank line), and a run of literal source newlines
  (leave exactly as the flat rendering has it). The first draft collapsed `\n{2,}` and
  silently un-fixed #2169's own accession; the unit test caught it, but only because
  that test existed.
- ⚠ **"Empty block" is a property of the block's CONTENT, not of its entity.** The
  second draft normalised `<p>&nbsp;</p>` and missed `<p><br/></p>`, which is the same
  rendered blank line written differently — found by the mandated Codex checkpoint-2
  pass, then measured rather than accepted: over the first 4,000 accessions the
  break-only block appears in 293 Item 403 candidate cells across 59 accessions, and
  `<br><br>` runs in 444 / 124. Enumerate what "empty" can be spelt as
  (`&nbsp;` / `&#160;` / `&#xa0;` / `<br>` / whitespace) before writing the predicate.
  Codex earning here is consistent with the file's own note that it pays on judgement
  artefacts: the finding was about the MODEL of a blank line, not a line of code.
- ⚠ **Blanking the resolved column is not enough when a recovery scan reads the other
  cells.** On `0001193125-26-140058` (Lamar) `_resolve_columns` puts `shares_idx` on an
  empty layout cell and the ragged-row recovery picks the amount out of cell 7. A
  row-level repair has to cover every cell of the row, not the one the resolver named.
- ⚠ **An unreachable guard reads as coverage it does not have — delete it.** An
  explicit `index != name_idx` exemption was written to keep the collapse off the
  holder name. The revert probe reported NOT CAUGHT, and the reason was that the stack
  gate (every line of the cell parses as an amount or a percent) already excludes a
  name, so no fixture can construct the case. Removed, and the reasoning moved into
  the docstring; the probe now attacks the gate that is actually load-bearing.
- ⚠ **An A/B harness that omits ONE writable column reports CLEAN while that column
  moves.** The skill's rule "arm 3 must cover fields the harness does NOT key on" was
  read as covering `holder_role` — the column #2164 burned — and `percent_of_class` was
  carried in the summary JSON but never compared. What exposed it was not the A/B: it
  was diffing two TREATMENT runs against each other to check that a performance
  short-circuit was behaviour-neutral, which surfaced nine fabricated percents on
  `0001213900-26-076369` that a mid-branch revision had been adding. The published
  arm-1 numbers had said `0 lost / 0 gained / 0 role drift` throughout. **Enumerate the
  writable columns from the row type, not from memory of which one bit last time**, and
  make the self-comparison (branch vs branch across a refactor) a routine arm — it is
  free once the control run exists and it is the only arm that catches a "no-op"
  optimisation that is not one.
- Enforced in: this prevention log;
  `scripts/ab_2358_def14a_line_structure.py::_diff` (the percent arm and the ⚠ on why
  it exists); `app/providers/implementations/sec_def14a.py::_strip_inline_html`
  (`block_breaks`,
  off by default, with the why-not-shared comment) + `_RawTable.line_rows` +
  `_collapse_stacked_value_cells`;
  `tests/test_sec_def14a_parser.py::TestBlockLevelLineStructure` (the SCT/scorer pin
  is `test_the_flat_grid_the_sct_path_reads_carries_no_tag_derived_newline` and
  `test_a_multi_line_header_caption_still_matches_its_prescribed_phrase`);
  `scripts/probe_2358_line_structure.py` (7/7 caught).

## A PR whose branch CONFLICTS never gets a CI run at all, and it looks exactly like an Actions outage (#2358, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: a push lands (`origin/<branch>` moves, `gh pr view` shows the new head), and then **no workflow run is ever created** — `gh pr checks` says `no checks reported`, `gh run list --branch` shows nothing for the new SHA, and there is nothing to `gh run rerun` because no run exists. Waited 35 minutes across two pushes. `githubstatus.com` read `operational` with no unresolved incidents, and the previous session's playbook for this shape (an empty commit to force event creation) did nothing.
- Root cause: every workflow in this repo triggers on `pull_request: branches: [main]`, and a `pull_request` event runs against the **merge ref**. When the branch conflicts with `main`, GitHub cannot compute that ref, so the event produces no run. `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n> --jq .mergeable` returned **false**. Two sibling loops merge into this repo, so `main` moves within the hour and a branch that was rebased 40 minutes ago is routinely stale.
- ⚠ **The discriminator is one API call, and the whole-repo view is what points at it.** `gh run list --limit 5` showed the SIBLING branch getting runs 20 seconds earlier — so run creation was healthy and the problem was mine. A branch-scoped poll cannot tell "Actions is down" from "this PR cannot be merged", and the previous session diagnosed a genuine outage from exactly the same branch-scoped evidence.
- Prevention: when checks do not appear within a few minutes of a push, run **both** of these before concluding anything about Actions — `gh api repos/.../pulls/<n> --jq .mergeable` (false → rebase and force-push, the run appears immediately) and `gh run list --limit 5` (other branches getting runs → it is not an outage). Only if run creation is dead repo-wide is the empty-commit recovery the right move. Corollary for this loop: **rebase immediately before every push, not once per session** — the instruction set already says so for review-bot accuracy, and this is the harder failure, because a stale base does not report a wrong finding, it reports nothing at all.
- Enforced in: this prevention log.

### When the published rule is an ALGORITHM rather than a number, its authoritative transcription is a reference implementation's source — adopt the formula without adopting the dependency (#2240 5e-2, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: criterion 3 names the method (*"a block bootstrap over calendar blocks with errors clustered by date"*) but not the block LENGTH, and picking one is the `.claude/CLAUDE.md` *"am I about to pick a threshold, ratio or window"* trigger. The plausible-looking answer — "about 20 days, roughly a holding period" — is invented, and is the same shape as #2279's invented 20th/80th-percentile BandWidth band where Bollinger's published rule is six months.
- Root cause of the near-miss: the rule that exists (**Politis & White 2004**, with the **Patton, Politis & White 2009** correction) is an *algorithm* — a lag-selection loop, a flat-top window, two aggregates and a scheme-dependent constant. A citation from memory gets the paper right and the arithmetic wrong, and the specific thing memory gets wrong here is silent: the constant is **2 for the stationary bootstrap and 4/3 for the circular one**, so a crossed pair mis-sizes every block while producing an entirely plausible number.
- ⚠ **The reuse check and the source check are the same step here.** `arch.bootstrap.optimal_block_length` implements it, and reading that function's source gave both the exact arithmetic AND its two DOIs. Neither `arch` nor `statsmodels` nor `scipy` is installed in this repo, and `arch` pulls scipy + statsmodels + pandas for one ~40-line formula — so the formula was transcribed and cited, and the dependency was not added. **Reading a library's source to get a published formula right is not the same decision as depending on it.**
- Prevention: when a spec names a METHOD but leaves a tuning parameter open, (1) search for the published *selection rule* before freezing a constant — for block bootstraps, bandwidths, lag lengths and kernel windows one almost always exists; (2) if the rule is an algorithm, transcribe it from a reference implementation's source, not from memory, and record the DOIs beside the code; (3) pin it with an **independent transcription in the test** that takes the scheme constant as an ARGUMENT and asserts the two schemes differ on the same series — otherwise the crossed-constant defect passes every test you would think to write.
- ⚠ Where genuinely no rule exists, the free constants must still be frozen behind a model id (`BOOTSTRAP_MODEL_ID`) so a stored number cannot change meaning silently — here that covers the resample count, the confidence level, the percentile-interval method, and the choice of an active-date rather than full-calendar cluster axis.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `app/services/block_bootstrap.py`'s header (both DOIs, the 4/3-vs-2 warning, and what each free constant is) and `optimal_block_length`; `tests/test_block_bootstrap.py::_reference_block_length` + `::test_it_matches_an_independent_transcription_of_the_published_formula`; `sql/265_strategy_results_block_bootstrap.sql`'s `bootstrap_block_length` comment; `scripts/probe_2240_block_bootstrap.py` probes 3 and 4.

## A predicate that takes one row's name can still be a TABLE-level test — grep the call sites before trusting the name (#2176, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: `Total`, `Common Stock` and `Series A Common Shares` stored in `def14a_beneficial_holdings` as beneficial owners, on a path that already owned a predicate for exactly that vocabulary. The issue's own filed hypothesis was that the guard was FAILING, and the natural next step is to debug the predicate.
- It is not failing. `_is_beneficial_owner_identity('Total')` returns `False` and always did. The predicate has **one** call site — inside `_owner_identity_fraction`, whose only consumer is the table-eligibility gate at `>= _ROW_IDENTITY_FLOOR` (0.5). It is never applied to a row. An ADMITTED table wrote every row it produced, and the floor tolerates 49% non-owners **by design**. There was no per-row layer at all.
- ⚠ **The shape is what generalises: a predicate whose signature is `(one item) -> bool` reads as an item filter, and this one is named, documented and unit-tested as a row test.** Its scope is a property of its CALL SITES, not of its signature. One `grep -n` for the symbol answered a question two sessions had reasoned about instead. Do that before designing anything around "why isn't the guard firing".
- ⚠ **Do not fix it by applying the POSITIVE predicate per row.** Measured over all 110,748 stored rows: it rejects 2,246 (1,306 distinct names) including bare `BlackRock`, `Margareth Øvrum` and the Item 403(b) Instruction 5 group row, and wipes 34 accessions to zero. The safe per-row layer is the NEGATIVE test (`_is_instrument_not_owner` — "every word is equity/award vocabulary"), which is the same closed vocabulary the table gate already trusts.
- ⚠ **An aggregate WORD is not a discriminator when the regulation REQUIRES an aggregate ROW.** 17 CFR 229.403(b) Instruction 5 mandates the directors-and-officers-as-a-group row, and issuers spell it `Total shares owned by executive officers and directors (13 persons)`. The widening that looks obvious — "the name CONTAINS the aggregate noun" — deletes the row the reg compels, so the test must stay "**every** word is instrument vocabulary". ⚠ The size of what it would delete is COMPUTED, not written down here: `census_2176_def14a_aggregate_rows.py` arm 5 re-derives it against a control parse, because a figure hand-copied into a log entry goes stale the moment the vocabulary moves and goes stale where a reader trusts it most. Cross-source (SEC EDGAR direct, `0000821130-25-000055`) shows why the junk side is nonetheless real: its `Total` row is a cross-class total for ONE holder and its Percent-of-Class cell is literally `N/A`; we stored it at 82.0%, scraped from the adjacent *Percent of Shares of Common Stock* column.
- ⚠ **When the fix that precedes yours has not been backfilled, a census over the TABLE measures the OLD parser.** 110,091 of 110,748 rows still carried `fetched_at = 2026-07-30`, pre-#2175/#2169. The issue's standing instruction was "re-measure after the backfill drains" — but the backfill is an operator step, and re-parsing the stored payloads is the same measurement without waiting for one. Check `fetched_at` before believing any census over a table whose writer just changed.
- ⚠ **Control and treatment A/B arms CAN run concurrently, and it halves a 5-hour wall clock.** Python imports the parser once at process start, so editing the module after launching the control arm does not reach the running process. Two conditions make it honest rather than lucky, and both are cheap: prove the control process's tree is parse-identical to the base (`git diff <control-commit> origin/main -- <parser>` → 0 lines), and confirm the corpus is not drifting under you (the harness's server-side cursor pins one MVCC snapshot per arm, and its `_diff` raises on a symmetric difference rather than intersecting).
- ⚠⚠ **A ROW FILTER placed upstream of a SELECTION gate is a selection change, and it fails in the admit direction where nothing is watching.** This is the lesson that cost two extra A/B rounds, and neither the unit tests, the four revert-probes nor a clean Codex review saw it. Two independent instances in ONE branch:
  1. **Via the extraction.** `_is_item403_eligible` scores `_owner_identity_fraction` over whatever `_extract_holder_rows` returns, so pruning non-owner rows RAISES every table's fraction. Tables that correctly failed `_ROW_IDENTITY_FLOOR` began clearing it: **+10 rows over 3 accessions, every one an Item 402 equity-compensation-plan row** ('Weighted Average Exercise Price', 'Total Shares Subject To Outstanding Awards'). The function's own docstring already warned that "row identity alone admits Item 402 compensation tables" — the guard quietly disarmed the limb that enforced it. Same failure mode as #2158.
  2. **Via a SHARED PREDICATE, which is the sneakier one.** `_is_beneficial_owner_identity` *short-circuits* on `_is_instrument_not_owner`, so widening the instrument predicate NARROWS owner identity, lowers the fraction and DE-admits tables. Making the class-designator strip unconditional took `0000062234-25-000015` from **2/3 = 0.667 to 1/3 = 0.333** and deleted the whole table — including its 229.403(b) Instruction 5 group row, the row the change exists to protect. Grep the predicate's callers before changing it; a helper named for one job is not private to it.
  - Prevention: a per-row filter gets a **keyword defaulting to OFF**, and the storage path is its only caller, so the selection path stays byte-identical to base. Then say which arm proves it: `GAINED 0` is the assertion, not `LOST n`.
  - ⚠ **The direction that matters is the one the A/B calls GAINED, and it is easy to skim past when the loss side looks right.** Round 1 read as a clean subtractive change on the loss side alone.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `app/providers/implementations/sec_def14a.py::_extract_holder_rows` (the per-row guard and its "deliberately the NEGATIVE test" comment), `_is_item403_eligible` (extracts with `drop_non_owner_rows=False` + the why-comment) and `_is_instrument_not_owner` (`strip_class_designator` default-off + the measured why); `tests/test_sec_def14a_parser.py::TestItem403RowIsABeneficialOwner` (`test_the_instruction_5_group_row_survives` is the bound, `test_a_bare_entity_name_without_a_corporate_designator_survives` is the anti-positive-predicate pin, `test_the_row_guard_is_not_a_table_selection_change` + `test_an_item_402_plan_table_is_not_admitted_by_pruning` + `test_the_designator_strip_does_not_de_admit_an_instruction_5_table` are the three selection-coupling pins); `scripts/probe_2176_item403_row_owner.py` (6/6 caught, each probe naming its bystanders); `scripts/census_2176_def14a_aggregate_rows.py` (arm 3 measures vocabulary extensions instead of choosing them; arm 5 sizes the widening NOT taken; `_guard_rejects` keeps the census on the GUARD's semantics rather than the eligibility one).

## A gate that reads the JOINED header condemns a table for ONE extra column — and the answer is the source's own STRUCTURE, not a fifth vocabulary patch (#2176 class 1, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: ExlService's Item 403(b) table (`0001193125-25-103261`, `0001193125-26-181891`) extracted **zero** holders while the 403(a) table immediately above it — whose header is byte-identical minus two columns — extracted fine. Measured on the control arm this session: 3 holders where the document has 16. The rejected captions are `Name and address | Shares | % | Vested but unsettled RSUs | Total`; `_item403_value_signature` joins every header cell and searches `_COMP_PCT_RE`, so the single word `Vested` in column 5 vetoes columns 3 and 4.
- ⚠ **The obvious fix is a trap, and it fails in the direction the ticket was not looking.** `_COMP_PCT_RE` detects a percent whose DENOMINATOR is compensation, and a denominator is a property of one COLUMN — so scoping the veto per-cell (veto unless a comp-free amount cell AND a comp-free percent cell survive) reads as the principled repair. Measured over 25,954 accessions it admitted **16 tables across 14 header shapes, essentially all Item 402** (`Total Dollar Value of Long-Term Incentive Award (100%)`, `Base Salary ($) | Incentive Target Percentage (%)`, `Time-based Awards (#) (50%) | Performance-based Awards (#) (50%)`) — and **de-admitted two literally-prescribed 229.403 tables on `0000100493-25-000114`** (Tyson: `Title of Class | Name and Address of Beneficial Owner | Amount and Nature of Beneficial Ownership | Percent of Class`, 3 + 22 holders). Not because the gate rejected them: a newly-eligible compensation table won an EARLIER window, so selection never reached the real one. Same window-flip shape as #2164's zero-width scrub. The looser variant (percent-only) was worse: 40 admitted, 9 de-admitted.
- ⚠ **A SELECTION change loses in a different accession from the one it gains in, so a net count cannot see it.** That variant read as **+59 extracted names** — a small, plausible widening. Diff the SELECTED SET per entity, not the totals. (Belongs in `.claude/skills/engineering/full-population-ab.md` §"Directionality"; ⚠ `.claude/skills/**` writes were denied on this worktree, so it is recorded here and still needs copying across.)
- Root cause of the class: **four prior fixes on this surface were vocabulary patches** (#2088 / #2094 / #2097 / #2169), and the fifth was due. The vocabulary is not the axis. 17 CFR 229.403 is ONE Item with TWO subsections — (a) >5% owners, (b) directors and management plus the Instruction 5 group row — and issuers render them as two tables under one heading, which is already why the window loop concatenates every eligible table rather than taking the best. Both subsections carry the reg's same prescribed captions, and Rule 13d-3(d)(1)(i) (17 CFR 240.13d-3) DEEMS a person the beneficial owner of securities they have a right to acquire, so 403(b) is commonly 403(a)'s header PLUS component columns. Admitting on that structure — captions a superset of an independently eligible table's, same window — fixes the class without touching the vocabulary, and **cannot re-rank window selection**, because it takes the eligible set as a precondition.
- ⚠ **"Require value evidence on the sibling too" deletes the case the ticket exists to fix.** Codex raised it at checkpoint 2 and it is the right instinct with the wrong threshold: the 403(b) table has 13 holders, 13 with a share count and **6 with a percent** (the NEOs carry one, the directors do not), so `_has_item403_value_rows` returns `False` at 6 < 6.5 and the data-row fallback cannot rescue the table either. 229.403 does not require a percent on every row. Run the predicate against the fixture before adopting a hardening that sounds strictly safer.
- ⚠ Worth knowing for anyone extending this: `_score_table_headers` returns **0** for any header carrying an `_ITEM_402_AWARD_MARKERS` caption, and `window_qualifying` filters `score >= _WINDOW_SCORE_FLOOR`, so grant-date / exercise-price / payout-value / value-realized tables can never reach the sibling path at all. The residual exposure is a comp table that repeats ALL of an eligible table's captions and carries no award marker — zero instances across the corpus.
- ⚠ **The dump-replay harness clips header tuples to 12 cells (`_MAX_HEADERS`) and that is visible in its fidelity gate, not hidden by it.** `0001140361-25-046376` / `-046469` carry an 18-cell header whose `Percent (2)` sits at index 13, so the replay reports 0 rows where the real parser returns 19. Two accessions of 25,954 — but a variant that fires only on a wide header would be invisible to the ranking, which is why the end-to-end A/B against a real `origin/main` worktree stays the authority.
- Also measured, and it falsified the issue: **class 3 was already fixed** before this change. The control arm returns **19 holders** on both `0001140361-25-046376` and `0001140361-25-046469` — exactly the count the issue records as lost — because the header extraction improved after the issue's `7b2ae45f` baseline. Re-measure a residual list against HEAD before designing for it.
- What the structural arm cost, end to end against a real `origin/main` worktree, all 42,705 stored `def14a_body` payloads re-parsed per arm: **LOST 0, GAINED 26 over 2 accessions**, 0 share drift, 0 percent drift, 0 role drift; arm 2 (parse vs STORED) **0 regressions**. Every one of the 26 is an ExlService director / officer or the Instruction 5 group row.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `app/providers/implementations/sec_def14a.py::_subsection_sibling_tables` (the 229.403 / 13d-3 rationale and the "cannot move window SELECTION" precondition), `_header_caption_set`, `_SUBSECTION_CAPTION_FLOOR` (which states plainly that the corpus does not distinguish 2 from 3); `tests/test_sec_def14a_parser.py::TestItem403SubsectionSiblings` (5 cases, 6/6 revert-probes, two of which were TEST faults first — a comp fixture scoring below the window floor, and a class-label fixture already deleted by #2373's per-row guard); `scripts/analyse_2176_comp_veto_scope.py` (the rejected arms are kept, measured, in the file).
- ⚠⚠ **Cost a corpus operation BEFORE firing it — a runbook's "allow hours" is prose, not a measurement.** #2358's OPERATOR VERIFY block said to trigger a source-wide `sec_rebuild` and *"allow hours"*. Measured on 2026-08-07 it is **2 to 28 days**: `sec_def14a` carries **117,075** manifest rows, and `sec_manifest_worker` runs `max_rows=200` per 5-minute tick (`app/workers/scheduler.py:5583`) **shared across every source by fair quota** (~13-16/tick/source), with ticks routinely lost to `fire suppressed (max_instances active)`. Ceiling if def14a took 100% of every tick ≈ 49 h; realistic ≈ 28 days. The ticket's actual acceptance criterion was **9 accessions**, which six `instrument_id`-scoped rebuilds reset in **216 rows / ~20 seconds**. The arithmetic is two queries — rows in scope, and the worker's per-tick budget — and it inverts the plan.
  - Prevention: before any `sec_rebuild` / rewash / backfill, divide **rows in scope** by **worker rows-per-hour** and write the number down. If a bug's blast radius is N accessions, scope the rebuild to those N subjects; a corpus-wide re-parse is a separate scheduled operation with its own ticket (filed as #2377), never a step inside a bug closure. It also starves every other source's drain for its duration, which nothing reports.
  - ⚠ **And `pgrep` for a sibling corpus job first — the rule already exists and was skipped here.** A source-wide rebuild was fired while the ownership loop held a full-population A/B on the same corpus. It was harmless *only* by mechanism: the A/B reads `filing_raw_documents` through a named cursor whose MVCC snapshot was fixed at its transaction start, and it writes to a file, not the DB. Had it read through fresh short transactions it would have been silently contaminated mid-run. `scripts/autonomy/loop_status.sh` shows loop iteration state and **nothing about what those iterations are running against the shared dev DB** — the heavy consumers were visible only in `pg_stat_activity`.
- ⚠⚠ **A scope/filter key can be STRUCTURALLY incapable of matching, and `status='completed'` hides it — verify a job by its own reset count, never by request status.** `POST /jobs/sec_rebuild/run` with `{"filer_cik": "<cik>", "source": "sec_def14a"}` returned `completed` six times and reset **zero** rows. `_resolve_scope` matches `filer_cik` against `subject_type IN ('institutional_filer','blockholder_filer')` only, while DEF 14A is **issuer**-scoped (`('issuer','1938','0000043920','sec_def14a')`) — so no CIK can ever match for `sec_def14a`, `sec_10k`, `sec_10q`, `sec_8k` or any issuer-scoped source. The module docstring documents the payload as *"all filings under that filer's CIK for the source"*, with no subject-type restriction, which is what I followed. Filed as #2379.
  - The only thing that noticed was `Row-count spike detected: sec_rebuild: row_count dropped from 4040 to 0` — a WARNING in a log nobody reads during an operator step. This is the class `.claude/CLAUDE.md` already names: *"a job that no-ops and reports success is invisible to every automated check we have."*
  - Prevention: after triggering any rebuild, assert the **job's own emitted counts** (`sec_rebuild: triples=N manifest_reset=N`) and a **row-level witness** — here, `last_attempted_at` on one known-affected accession, which was still `2026-07-19` while the request said `completed`. A `completed` status is evidence the code ran, not evidence it did anything. Correct issuer-scoped form is `{"instrument_id": <id>, "source": "..."}`, verified: 6 rebuilds, `manifest_reset` 35+53+44+41+23+20 = **216**, matching `pending=216` exactly.
### Two correct statistics can be joined into a wrong one by their AXIS, and neither side's tests can see it (#2240 5e-3, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: criterion 6's Deflated Sharpe takes four inputs — `SR`, skew, kurtosis and a sample length `T` — and §5.2 says it CONSUMES criterion 3's effective sample size. Both quantities already existed and both were correct: `StrategyMetrics.sharpe` is an annualised Sharpe of the equity curve's per-period returns (5d), and `effective_sample_size` is a Kish ESS in units of **trades** (5e-2). Wiring the obvious pair together — the Sharpe that is already on the row, the sample size the spec names — produces a statistic where the numerator is per-period and `sqrt(T-1)` counts trades. It computes, it is in `[0, 1]`, and it looks exactly like a DSR.
- Root cause: Bailey & López de Prado eq. (2) divides a Sharpe by the estimated standard error **of that same Sharpe**, built from that same series' third and fourth moments and that same series' length. The equation is only meaningful when all four inputs describe ONE series. Nothing in either producing module says which axis its number lives on, because on its own each is unambiguous — the ambiguity is created by the join, and the join is in a third module.
- ⚠ **No test on either side can catch this.** 5d's tests pin an annualised Sharpe against an annualised expectation; 5e-2's pin ESS × deff == trade_count. Both keep passing. The defect exists only in the consumer, and a consumer test written from the same misunderstanding asserts the wrong thing confidently.
- ⚠ The unit trap is visible in the source rule and nowhere else: the paper's own worked example de-annualises everything (`2.5/√250`, `V = 1/(2·250)`, `T = 1250`), which is the sentence that settles the axis. **Reading the paper's numerical example, not just its equations, is what surfaced it.**
- Prevention: when a formula consumes two or more quantities produced by different modules, state the AXIS (per-trade / per-period / per-instrument) of each input in the consumer's header and pick ONE, then bind it structurally rather than by convention. Concretely here: the DSR is computed on the trade axis because the ESS is in trades; the per-trade Sharpe is stored under a DIFFERENT column name from the annualised one (`dsr_trade_sharpe` vs `sharpe`) so no reader can substitute one for the other; and `StrategyResult.__post_init__` refuses a DSR whose `effective_sample_size` disagrees with the metric set's, because there is only one column for that number and the round trip would otherwise silently replace one with the other. ⚠ That last invariant was found BY the round-trip test, not by review — a save/load cycle is what makes "two copies of one number" visible.
- ⚠ Corollary for the verification harness: assert the axis by CONTRAST, not by equality. `verify_2240_statistics.py` P9 recomputes the DSR on the nominal trade count purely to require it comes out strictly higher — a contrast that did not move would mean the ESS was never wired in, which an equality check against a stored value cannot detect.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `app/services/deflated_sharpe.py`'s header (the per-observation warning and the axis decision, with the rejected alternative); `sql/266_strategy_results_deflated_sharpe.sql`'s `dsr_trade_sharpe` comment; `app/services/strategy_result.py::StrategyResult.__post_init__` (the one-sample-size-one-column check); `tests/test_deflated_sharpe.py::TestEffectiveSampleSizeIsTheSampleLength`; `tests/test_strategy_holdout_namespace.py::test_a_result_carrying_the_criterion_6_block_survives_the_round_trip`; `scripts/verify_2240_statistics.py` P9; `scripts/probe_2240_deflated_sharpe.py` probes 1 and 16.

## A control arm whose random draw sits in an uncorrelated scalar subquery is an InitPlan — evaluated ONCE, and it certifies whatever you point it at (#2231, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: a placebo arm for the #2231 split detector — "same 931 bracket windows, but a randomly drawn instrument instead of the real one" — returned **0 hits of 931** against the real arm's 490. Read as a perfect separation and a decisive result. It was a constant. The draw lived in a `SELECT` -list scalar subquery with no outer reference (`(SELECT p.instrument_id FROM present p WHERE p.rn = 1 + floor(random()*(SELECT max(n) FROM present))::int)`), which Postgres hoists to an **InitPlan** and evaluates once for the whole query, so all 931 rows shared one fake instrument. Drawing per row in the outer query and joining gives **32 of 931 (3.4%)** and **852 distinct fakes**.
- ⚠ The failure is silent in the direction that flatters you: a degenerate control produces `0`, and `0` is exactly what a working control looks like when the signal is real. There is no error, no warning, and the number is the one you were hoping for.
- Prevention: any randomised control must report **how many distinct draws it made**, not just its hit count. `count(DISTINCT fake_key)` next to the hit count would have shown `1` immediately. Structurally: compute the random key in the outer query (or a `LATERAL`), never inside an uncorrelated scalar subquery, and never inside a CTE Postgres can treat as an InitPlan. This generalises past `random()` to any volatile function used as a per-row generator — `clock_timestamp()`, `gen_random_uuid()`, `nextval()` behave the same way at that position.
- Same session, same shape, different mechanism: a covariate test on `financial_facts_raw.decimals` reported `decimals_changed = False` on **every** pair and was taken as "presentation scale never changes". The column is **empty on all 6,508,601 rows** — `data.sec.gov` companyfacts entries carry no `decimals` key, so the writer at `app/providers/implementations/sec_fundamentals.py:509` (`str(entry["decimals"]) if "decimals" in entry else None`) always stores `NULL`. A probe over a uniformly-NULL column matches nothing and proves nothing. **Check a column is populated before drawing a conclusion from its uniformity** — one `count(*) FILTER (WHERE col IS NOT NULL)`.

## A corroboration source with no RATIO corroborates the ENTITY, not the EVENT (#2231, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: FINRA's `stock_split_flag = 'S'` was adopted as the independent arm for the #2231 XBRL split detector's false-positive rate. On the continuous-coverage window (2025-04-30 → 2026-07-15; **30 held settlement dates against 29.0 expected bimonthly**, so coverage is complete there) it corroborated **316 of 574** detected clusters (55.1%) against a placebo of **17 of 574** (3.0%). Read as a per-event precision of 55%.
- It is not a per-event anything. FINRA's flag says *a split happened to this security in this period*; it carries **no ratio**. Those 316 corroborated clusters stand on only **233 distinct instruments** (1.36 clusters per instrument; 59 instruments carry 2-5 distinct ratios inside one window), so at most **233/574 = 40.6%** are individually attested and the other 83 ride a sibling cluster's flag. A detector that emitted three wrong ratios and one right one on the same instrument would score 4/4.
- ⚠ The consequence bit us immediately: a discriminator built to strip the detector's largest false-positive class was tested on this arm and **ordered backwards** — `admitted` 54.0% vs `scale_artefact` 59.8% vs `both_inconsistent` 75.0%. That is not evidence the rule is wrong; it is evidence the arm cannot see the rule, because an instrument with messy filings is also disproportionately an instrument that really split. Adopting the rule on its 21x artefact-reduction alone, or rejecting it on this ordering, would both have been wrong.
- Prevention: before adopting a corroboration source, ask **what key it can attribute on**. If its granularity is coarser than the thing being validated (entity vs event, day vs intraday, filing vs row), it bounds *existence*, never *precision*, and must be reported as an entity-level rate with its placebo — never as a false-positive rate. Where no ratio-carrying source exists, the honest substitute is a **labelled subset from public record**: six 2024 forward splits picked without reference to our data (WMT 3:1, NVDA 10:1, CMG 50:1, AVGO 10:1, SMCI 10:1, LRCX 10:1) were recovered 6/6 at the exact contractual ratio, which is a precision statement the instrument-level arm cannot make.
- ⚠ Those same six carry **zero** FINRA flags, and that is a coverage artefact, not a semantic one — all six effective dates fall in our FINRA gap (we hold 2024-01-12/01-31/02-15 then nothing until 2025-04-30). "Source X does not report Y" requires checking that source X's coverage includes Y's date first.

## Before designing a new table, grep for it — a sibling epic may have shipped it four days ago (#2231, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: the #2231 spec opened with *"There is no splits or corporate-actions table anywhere in the schema"*, which was true when written on 2026-08-03. `sql/246_price_adjustments_and_series_breaks.sql` (#2261, phase 0a of #2240, from the S7 verdict on #2247) landed **`price_adjustments`** and **`price_series_break`** and was applied to dev. `price_adjustments` reserves `source = 'sec_xbrl' (#2231)` **by name** — the TA epic designed the table expecting this detector to feed it — and supplies most of what two of the spec's open Codex items asked for: `adjustment_id` PK, `superseded_by`/`superseded_at` append-only correction state, `source_priority` arbitration, `detector_version` as rule-set-id-plus-code-hash, `observed_at` as a replay pin, and a partial unique index forcing exactly one active row per `(instrument_id, effective_date)`. ⚠ **Not everything**: `source_document_id` is singular where a detector cluster rests on several accessions, `kind` is unconstrained `TEXT` with no CHECK, and the active-row index keys on an exact date — so it does not give event identity to a detector that emits brackets. Adoption removes the need for a second table; it does not close the open items on its own.
- ⚠ Two loops now merge into this repo. A "no such table exists" premise has a **half-life measured in days**, and the schema is the one place where a stale premise produces a duplicate rather than an error — nothing fails, you just get two tables for one concept and a silent arbitration problem later.
- Prevention: a spec that proposes a new table re-greps `sql/` and `information_schema.tables` **at push time**, not at authoring time, and the reproduction section records the date of the check. Cheapest form: `SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name ~ '<concept>'` plus `grep -rln "<concept>" sql/ app/`.
- ⚠ Adoption is not free and the gap is worth naming: `price_adjustments.effective_date` is a single DATE ("first bar at the NEW scale") and the XBRL detector produces a **bracket** (median 207 days). There is nowhere in `sql/246` to record that uncertainty, and its active-row unique index is keyed on the exact date, so two detectors bracketing the same split differently would not collide. Cross-epic contract gaps like that are surfaced to both owners, not resolved unilaterally by whichever loop noticed.
### A bound declared on one axis, applied to a window cut on another (#2240 5e-4, 2026-08-07)

- Second instance of the class the 5e-3 entry above names, in a different shape: 5e-3 was two statistics JOINED on mismatched axes; this is one CONSTANT declared on axis A and applied to a window cut on axis B. The join is what made 5e-3 visible. Here there is no join — the constant is simply used, and it type-checks, and it is the right order of magnitude.
- Symptom: §5.3 of the bounded-backtester spec fixed the walk-forward embargo as *"the embargo is `max_hold_bars` wherever one is declared — S-3: 10 and S-4: 40"*. `max_hold_bars` counts an **instrument's own bars** — the resolver scans forward through the series it was handed. Walk-forward folds are cut on the **panel axis**, the union of every instrument's trading dates. An instrument's dates are a SUBSET of the panel's, so a hold of `h` instrument bars spans `h` panel dates **or more**, never fewer. An embargo of 10 panel bars therefore under-covers a 10-instrument-bar hold — in the direction that leaks.
- ⚠ **Measured before it was asserted, and it is rare rather than theoretical**: over 2,456,097 S-1 in-sample positions the panel span exceeded `bars_held` on **3** of them, by up to **374 dates**; over 22,811 S-3 positions, on **0**. A 3-in-2.5-million defect is exactly the shape no fixture produces and no sampled check finds — and the whole point of an embargo is to cover the tail, so the three positions it misses are the population it exists for.
- Root cause of the class: a bound is written down in the units of whatever produced it, and applied in the units of whatever consumes it, with no sentence anywhere naming either. Both modules are individually correct and neither has a test that could fail.
- Prevention: **measure a bound on the axis the WINDOW is cut on, not on the axis the quantity was declared on** — the mismatch then cannot exist, rather than being corrected for. Concretely here: `walk_forward.training_embargo_bars` measures the maximum panel-axis label span over the fold's own post-purge training set, which needs no declared constant for any strategy and subsumes `max_hold_bars` (a strategy declaring one must measure a span at least that large — asserted as F4 by `scripts/verify_2240_walk_forward.py`, which also prints the realised excess so the assertion cannot be vacuously true).
- ⚠ Corollary, and it is the cheaper half of the lesson: **report the two axes side by side in the verification arm** even when you expect them to agree. The `panel − instrument span` line costs one Counter and is what turned "this is theoretically under-covered" into "3 positions, max 374 dates". Without it the correction would have shipped as reasoning, which is the thing this repo's rules say not to trust.
- ⚠ Related, and worth separating from the above: **"it needs an explicit call" can be an unstarted measurement wearing a status.** §5.3 carried S-1's embargo as blocked on a strategy-identity decision across three run reports. It was one query and an if-then, both writable in advance; measured, it took the branch that changes no identity at all. Already a `.claude/CLAUDE.md` rule (*"Answer the question yourself when you hold the facts"*) — this is its second confirmed instance.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `app/services/walk_forward.py`'s header (the axis warning and the measured-embargo construction, with §5.3's two rejected candidates and why the surviving one is not a third); `docs/proposals/ta/2026-08-07-bounded-backtester.md` §5.3 (the correction and the full-population table) and §8.4 (which constants are AFML's and which are ours); `scripts/verify_2240_walk_forward.py` F4 and the `panel − instrument span` report; `scripts/probe_2240_walk_forward.py` probes 5, 6 and 8.

## A magnitude floor and a roundness guard are PROXIES FOR EVIDENCE — when the source states the relationship structurally, retire them for that population (#2230, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: `_reconcile_insider_control_groups` (#1652) collapses a Section 16 deemed block that several related CIKs each report in full, gated on the shared value being **non-round** and **≥1,000,000**. Measured on the full population today, **627** cross-accession all-10%-owner equal-value insider clusters exist; **402** pass those gates and **225** do not. The 225 are not marginal cases — they include a 16-CIK Blackstone chain on `LGN` at 958,692 (rejected for being 41,308 shares under the floor) and a 9-CIK Starwood chain on `TRTX` at 12,000,000 (rejected for being an exact multiple of 100,000). Nothing about either is ambiguous to a human reader.
- Root cause is stated in the repo's own code and had not been acted on. `_reconcile_same_accession_groups`'s docstring (#1764) says a shared accession "IS the group evidence #1652/#1645 must infer", so that pass "needs **NO** magnitude floor or roundness proxy — those guards exist only to substitute for the membership evidence that a shared accession already provides." The guards are therefore not truths about deemed ownership; they are stand-ins. Anywhere else equally direct evidence exists, they are answering a question that has already been answered.
- ⚠ **An inherited root-cause was wrong in a way that changed the fix.** A prior session's handoff stated "378 clusters are entirely invisible to #1652", derived by modelling #1652 as `_collapse_same_accession_channel` — which is keyed `(winning_accession, shares)` and belongs to **#1764**. The actual #1652 pass buckets on `shares` alone and *is* cross-accession. Re-running the discriminator gave a different residual (**225**) with a different cause (the value proxies, not accession adjacency), so a fix built on the handoff would have targeted the wrong gate. Working-order step 3c exists for exactly this; the check is one query.
- Prevention: before loosening or patching an inference gate, ask **what evidence the gate is standing in for**, then look for that evidence in the source's own structured fields. Here two existed and neither had been consulted: the Form 3/4 relationship box `is_ten_percent_owner` (`insider_filers`), and Form 4 Table I column 5 Direct/Indirect (already stored as `ownership_nature`). Enforced in: `app/services/ownership_rollup.py::_is_deemed_chain` + the `_DEEMED_CHAIN_*` header; `tests/test_insider_deemed_chain_collapse.py`; `scripts/ab_2230_deemed_chain.py`.

## A classifier's false-positive class is a MEASUREMENT — name-shape and shared-address both failed it here, in opposite directions (#2230, 2026-08-07)

- Two plausible discriminators for "is this equal-value cluster a deemed chain or a coincidence" were tested on the full residual and both are falsified. Recording them so the next session does not re-derive either.
- **Entity name-shape** (LLC / L.P. / Trust / Partners / …) was the prior session's proposed admission test. It mis-classifies in both directions: `XFOR`'s 13-identity cluster at exactly 2,000,000 was catalogued as the equal-grant false-positive class because it reads as a list of individuals — it is `New Enterprise Associates 16, L.P.` plus twelve NEA managing members, a textbook Rule 16a-1(a)(2) chain and a **true positive**. Conversely `XPRO`'s four `Trust ulw Janice P. Mosing fbo <different child>` rows and `GSHD`'s four `<name> Jones Trust` rows are entity-named and are equal family distributions, **false positives**.
- **Shared filing address** (`insider_filers.street1`/`zip_code`) fails because officers and directors file from the ISSUER's address. `TEAM`'s two co-founders — the canonical false positive — share `c/o atlassian corporation`, while the genuine Starwood group on `TRTX` spans three addresses. Of the 225 residual clusters, 128 share one address and 96 do not, and the split does not track truth.
- What did discriminate is the pair of structured Form 3/4 fields, and each is load-bearing on its own: dropping the `is_ten_percent_owner` requirement admits **26** further clusters that are overwhelmingly equal DIRECTOR grants (`FLG` 11,220 across 11 CIKs, `BBT` 2,595 across 10, `NWFL` 825 across 8) — the #1659 class; and the Direct/Indirect shape is what separates a control chain (one direct holder, N indirect deemed owners) from equal family trusts (all direct).
- ⚠ The Form 3/4 "Other (specify)" box does carry explicit declarations — `member of a group` (851), `member of 10% owner group` (895), `member of 13(d) group` (245), 3,044 rows over 66 distinct forms. It reaches only **5 of the 627** clusters, so it is a corroborator, not a gate. Worth knowing it exists; not worth building on.
- Prevention: state the false-positive class as a query over the full population and read its members BY NAME before adopting a discriminator. A discriminator that has not been shown what it wrongly admits *and* what it wrongly rejects has been assumed, not measured.

## Postgres `\b` in a regex is BACKSPACE, not a word boundary — the pattern matches nothing and the zero reads as a finding (#2230, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: testing whether Form 3/4 filers declare group membership, `other_text ~* '(member[s]?\s+of\b.*\bgroup|\bgroup\s+member)'` returned **0 rows** — across the whole table, and across all 627 candidate clusters. Read for a moment as a clean negative result: "the declaration is never present on this population." A `GROUP BY lower(btrim(other_text))` on the same column moments earlier had shown `member of a group` with 851 rows, which is what made it obviously wrong.
- Root cause: Postgres ARE (POSIX Advanced Regular Expressions) follows the POSIX convention where `\b` is the **backspace character** (`\010`). The word-boundary escape is `\y` (`\m` / `\M` for start/end). PCRE-shaped patterns pasted from other languages therefore fail silently rather than erroring. Measured on this column: the `\b` form matches **0**, the `\y` form matches **2,921**.
- ⚠ The failure mode is the dangerous one — it returns the empty set, not an error, so it looks like evidence of absence. Same shape as the InitPlan placebo above and the empty-`decimals` covariate: **a probe that matches nothing proves nothing, and zero is the most persuasive wrong answer.**
- Prevention: any regex predicate written to CHARACTERISE a population must first be shown to match a known-present example. One line: run the pattern against a value you have already seen in a `GROUP BY` of the same column, and assert it is non-zero, before trusting any count derived from it. In Postgres specifically, prefer `\y` or drop the boundary entirely.

## ⚠ PENDING SKILL EDIT — the data-engineer I17 "`<memberOfGroup>` is empirically ABSENT" claim is FALSE and must be struck (#2230, 2026-08-07)

- `.claude/skills/data-engineer/SKILL.md` line 58 (invariant I17) reads *"**Never depend on `<memberOfGroup>`** — the element is empirically ABSENT from modern 13D XML; the legacy `blockholder_filings.member_of_group` column is noise."* The first clause is false as of today's dev DB.
- Measured this session: `select member_of_group, count(*), min(filed_at)::date from blockholder_filings group by 1` → `b` **29,876** · `a` **9,098** · NULL **68,973**, total 107,947. So **38,974 rows (36.1%) carry the element**, parsed at `app/providers/implementations/sec_13dg.py:430`. `min(filed_at)` is `2024-12-18` on all three buckets — the whole table sits above the 13D/G structured-XML mandate floor, which is why the absence claim (written 2026-06-16, #1645) no longer holds.
- ⚠ **The I17 CONCLUSION still stands and must not be weakened**: presence is not usefulness. The 'a'/'b'-both-appear-for-real-groups noise finding was NOT re-tested this session, and nothing here licenses depending on the column. Strike only the absence clause; keep "never depend on it".
- Writes to `.claude/skills/**` were DENIED on this worktree again this run (the #2376 permission friction, third occurrence). Apply the edit on a session that has permission.

## A census wrapped on a SHARED helper attributes its findings to the wrong pass — capture the ROUTE from the caller, never re-derive it from the gate (#2385, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: instrumenting `_collapse_insider_control_group` to census which clusters the rollup folds, the tier was recomputed from the module's own thresholds — `value_proxy` when `shares >= _INSIDER_GROUP_MIN_SHARES and _is_group_block(shares)`, else `deemed_chain`. On a 40-instrument smoke probe that reported an `AMR` cluster of 5 members, all `direct`, zero `indirect`, as a **`deemed_chain`** fold. `_is_deemed_chain` requires `n_indirect >= 2`, so it cannot have admitted that cluster; the label was impossible on its face.
- Root cause: `_collapse_insider_control_group` has **two** callers, not one — `_reconcile_same_accession_groups` (#1764, `app/services/ownership_rollup.py:2675`) and `_reconcile_insider_control_groups` (#1652/#2230, `:2820`) — and the same-accession pass runs FIRST (`:4207` before `:4208`). Every same-accession fold was therefore being scored against a gate that never saw it, and the "else" branch of a two-way tier split swept them all into `deemed_chain`.
- ⚠ The failure is silent in the direction that matters. Had the injected route been the one with the LOOSER gate, the mislabelled folds would have landed in a plausible bucket and the census would have read as clean. The tell here was an internally impossible combination, which is luck, not method.
- Prevention: when instrumenting a shared helper, `grep` for **every** caller first and record the route as data passed in from the caller (wrap the callers, set a flag). Re-deriving the caller's decision from its thresholds is a second implementation of that decision, and the two drift the moment a third caller appears. Enforced in: `scripts/audit_2385_control_group_rep.py::_tier` (takes `route`; the value thresholds only split the cross-accession route's own two tiers).

## A test that re-spells a shared sort key INLINE is a copy, and a copy drifts when the key gains a component (#2385, 2026-08-07)

- `tests/test_insider_deemed_chain_collapse.py::test_fold_is_allowed_when_the_other_row_belongs_to_the_REP` verifies that a fold is permitted when the other-channel row belongs to the cluster's representative. To find the rep it wrote the key out by hand: `max(holders, key=lambda h: (True, h.shares, h.filer_cik or "", h.winning_accession))`.
- #2385 adds a component to `_control_group_rep_key`. The inline copy does not have it, so the test would have attached its 13F row to a holder that is no longer the rep — i.e. it would have set up the OPPOSITE scenario from the one its name and docstring describe, while continuing to assert on the same output.
- Here it happened to fail loudly (the mis-targeted row makes the fold refused, so `corrs == []` and the assertion trips). That is a property of this test's shape, not of the pattern: a copy that lands on the same answer by coincidence keeps passing and stops testing anything.
- This is the mirror of the "a reference that IMPORTS the constant it validates is a tautology" entry (#2240 phase 5c). Both are about the boundary between a test and the thing under test: importing the constant proves nothing, copying it proves the wrong thing. The rule that survives both is **ask the module for its decision, assert on the CONSEQUENCE** — call `_control_group_rep_key`, then assert the resulting label/fold is what the source rule requires.
- Prevention: `grep` a new sort/priority key for inline re-spellings before changing it (`key=lambda` over the same fields is the shape to look for). Enforced in: `tests/test_insider_deemed_chain_collapse.py`, which now calls `_control_group_rep_key` instead of re-spelling it.

## `ownership_nature` is an OVERLOADED column — `direct` means Table I column 5 on 69,631 rows and "is an officer" on 3,404 (#2385, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: #2385 proposed preferring the Rule 16a-1(a)(2) **direct** holder as a control-group cluster's representative, reading `Holder.ownership_nature == "direct"`. Implemented literally that moves **224** folds of 1,433, and **59 of them promote the wrong holder** — the census surfaced `Wolfe Lauren Taylor`, `SCOTT JAMES R`, `MADAR JEAN` as the new label for an entity's block, which is precisely the defect the ticket exists to remove.
- Root cause: four writers populate the column and only three of them mean the same thing by it. `ownership_observations_sync.py:299`, `insider_form3_ingest.py:491` and `insider_transactions.py:1667` all derive it from the XML (`"indirect" if direct_indirect == "I" else "direct"`). `sec_insider_dataset_ingest.py::_map_relationship` (`:184`) maps the DERA insider dataset's **relationship flags** onto the same column instead — officer/director → `direct`, ten-percent-owner → `beneficial`, no flag → `direct` — and never reads `directOrIndirectOwnership` at all.
- Measured, full population (`ownership_insiders_current`, dev DB, 2026-08-07):

  ```sql
  SELECT ownership_nature, (source_document_id !~ ':(NDT|NDH):') AS from_table_i,
         count(*) FROM ownership_insiders_current GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;
  ```

  `direct`/true **69,631** · `direct`/false **3,404** · `indirect`/true **16,521** · `beneficial`/false **3,759**. So `beneficial` is 100% role-derived, `indirect` is 100% Table I, and **only `direct` is ambiguous** — ambiguous in the direction that promotes a natural person over the entity.
- ⚠ The trap is that the string is not wrong, it is *differently sourced*, so every local check passes: the value is in the schema CHECK enum, it round-trips, and the reading code is correct about what the column is named. Nothing short of asking WHERE THE ROW CAME FROM separates them. The discriminator already existed in the read path (the insiders query filters `:(NDT|NDH):` rows where a manifest parse exists) and had simply never been surfaced onto the `Holder`.
- ⚠⚠ **`_is_deemed_chain` (#2230) has the same exposure and is NOT fixed by #2385.** It counts `n_direct`/`n_indirect` off the same column to test the "≤1 direct, ≥2 indirect" control-chain shape, so a DERA officer row counts toward `n_direct` and can push a genuine chain past `_DEEMED_CHAIN_MAX_DIRECT`, while `beneficial` counts toward neither side. Filed separately — do not assume the provenance gate on the rep key covers it.
- Prevention: before branching on an enum-valued column, `grep` for **every writer** and confirm they agree on its meaning; a column with more than one producer is a union type until proven otherwise. Recorded in: `scripts/audit_2385_control_group_rep.py::_ungated_rep_key` (carries the falsification and the `source_document_id !~ ':(NDT|NDH):'` discriminator) and #2386. ⚠ No read-path consumer gates on provenance yet — #2385 shipped the MEASUREMENT only, because the rep-key change it was measuring turned out not to be display-only (see the entry below).

## ⚠ PENDING SKILL EDIT — `sec-edgar.md` §2.3 must record that `ownership_nature` is overloaded (#2385, 2026-08-07)

- `.claude/skills/data-sources/sec-edgar.md:322` documents `directOrIndirectOwnership` (`D`/`I`) and says both surface separately. True of the FORM. It says nothing about our stored column having a second, incompatible producer, which is the fact a reader actually needs before branching on it.
- Writes to `.claude/skills/**` were **DENIED on this worktree again** (#2376, fourth occurrence). Apply on a session that has permission. The edit is: after the existing `directOrIndirectOwnership` paragraph, add the four-writer split, the measured 69,631 / 3,404 / 16,521 / 3,759 table with the query above, the `source_document_id !~ ':(NDT|NDH):'` discriminator, and the rule "any read-path branch on `ownership_nature == 'direct'` must also check provenance — `ownership_rollup.Holder.nature_from_table_i` carries it".

## A dedup pass's REPRESENTATIVE is not a label — it is the identity that survives, so changing it re-parents every folded member's other-channel rows (#2385, 2026-08-07)

- #2385 was filed as **"Display-only — the wedge total is unaffected"**, on the reasoning that a control-group fold emits the same `shares_removed` whichever member it keeps. That is true of the fold in isolation and false of the rollup. Measured with a paired full-population A/B (control = a worktree at `origin/main`, treatment = the branch, both arms 2,178 instruments, **0 harness errors**): **108 instruments' pie totals move and 1,308,852,857 shares are removed net.**
- Two couplings make the rep load-bearing, and neither is visible from `_collapse_insider_control_group`:
  1. The rep is the one member **exempt** from the release-hazard check in `_reconcile_insider_control_groups` (`app/services/ownership_rollup.py`), so changing it changes which clusters fold at all.
  2. The rep is the identity that survives into `_reconcile_owner_once`. Every folded member is removed from `survivors`, which **releases that member's 13F / 13D rows** into their own wedges as standalone owners (the hazard #2229/#2230 already documented). So the rep choice decides whose cross-channel footprint stays merged and whose is set loose.
- The direction is mostly right and is not uniformly right, which is the part a net figure hides. `USBC`: rep moves from `Kidd Robert Gregory` (an individual, winning only on CIK order) to `Goldeneye 1995 LLC`, and the insiders wedge falls **737,776,188 → 379,961,188**. `ACDC`: rep moves from `THRC Management, LLC` to `THRC Holdings, LP` — correct by the source rule, since the LP holds directly and the LLC is the deemed manager — and the insiders wedge **rises 225,951,558 → 298,774,575**, because the demoted LLC is the member that held the other-channel rows. 66 instruments improve on the loss side alone, 19 regress, 94 are clean swaps.
- ⚠ **Do not read the net as the verdict.** The 1.3B removal rests on the release hazard happening to resolve favourably, not on a source rule. #2230 fenced that hazard for its own tier ONLY and recorded why: claiming a folded member's other rows would require reversing #1652's exact-value-only consumption rule, which is "a bigger decision than this ticket". A rep-selection change re-opens the hazard on the other two routes (931 same-accession + 488 value-proxy folds of 1,433) where no fence exists.
- Prevention: before changing a tie-break, selection key or "which one do we keep" rule inside a dedup/collapse pass, `grep` for every consumer of the SURVIVING object — not just the ones that read the field you are changing. If any downstream pass groups by that identity, the choice is arithmetic, not presentation, and needs the paired A/B. The tell that it was arithmetic here was cheap and was available before any code changed: `max(holders, key=_control_group_rep_key)` appears in a **gate**, not only in the collapse.

## A census that reads its CONTROL arm off the loaded function erases its own evidence the moment the fix lands (#2386, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: `scripts/audit_2386_deemed_chain_gate.py` wraps `_is_deemed_chain` and compares the current counting rule against a proposed one. The first draft took `verdict_now` from the wrapped function itself and computed only `verdict_gated`. That is correct exactly once — while the checkout still implements the old rule. Run the same script after the fix merges and the loaded gate IS the new rule, so `flips` collapses to 0 and the summary reads `admitted NOW == admitted under PROVENANCE GATE`. **The failure mode is that a broken measurement and a clean result are the same output.** Nothing errors, no count looks odd, and the script is checked in for the next session to re-run.
- Root cause: the harness treated "what the code does" as an observable it could read at run time, when it is a property of the COMMIT. A/B harnesses that shell out to a control worktree (`scripts/ab_2230_deemed_chain.py`) do not have this problem because the control is a separate process at a pinned SHA; an in-process census does, and looks simpler for it.
- Prevention: an in-process A/B must **compute both arms itself** from the module's constants, and record the loaded function's verdict as a THIRD field reconciled in the summary (`loaded gate agrees with UNGATED counting: N/N` / `… with PROVENANCE-gated: N/N`). That line is what tells the reader which arm the checkout implements, instead of leaving it to be assumed. Enforced in: `scripts/audit_2386_deemed_chain_gate.py::recording_gate` (the reconciliation print and the comment explaining it).
- ⚠ Related and already burned once on this ticket: the census had to wrap the **gate**, not the collapse. `scripts/audit_2385_control_group_rep.py` wraps `_collapse_insider_control_group`, which by construction cannot see a REFUSED cluster — and refusals were the entire population #2386 is about. When a ticket is about coverage (things wrongly rejected), instrument the predicate; a census on the accept path measures the complement of the question.

## A distorted counter inside a gate is not automatically a behaviour defect — measure WHICH precondition binds before writing an impact claim (#2386, 2026-08-07)

- `_is_deemed_chain` counts `n_direct`/`n_indirect` off `ownership_nature`, which has four writers and three meanings (see the #2385 entry above): `sec_insider_dataset_ingest._map_relationship` maps DERA RELATIONSHIP flags onto the same column, so a role-derived officer row counts toward `n_direct` and can push a genuine Rule 16a-1(a)(2) chain past `_DEEMED_CHAIN_MAX_DIRECT`. The counter really is wrong, and it is wrong at scale.
- Measured on the full population — `PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m scripts.audit_2386_deemed_chain_gate --out /tmp/audit2386.jsonl`, 2,178 instruments, **30,760 gate evaluations, 0 harness errors**: **1,465** evaluations carry at least one role-derived member and **866** have a nature count that MOVES under provenance gating (`n_direct` `1→0` on 836 of them). And **0 verdict flips.**
- The reason is the gate's evaluation order, which no amount of reasoning about the counter would have surfaced: of those 1,465, **1,455** are already refused for holding fewer than `_DEEMED_CHAIN_MIN_CIKS` distinct CIKs and **9** for failing the Form 3/4 10%-owner box. Exactly **one** clears both preconditions — `ACTU` at 196,428 (`Kreis Leslie W.` indirect/Table I + two Bios co-invest LPs whose `direct` is DERA-derived) — and it is refused under BOTH counting rules, because gating drops `n_direct` 2→0 but leaves `n_indirect` at 1, under the `>= 2` floor. `n_indirect` never moves anywhere in the population: `indirect` is 100% Table I-sourced.
- Prevention: when a ticket says "this counter is read off the wrong thing", the impact claim is not the count of affected rows — it is the count of DECISIONS that change, and those are separated by every other clause in the predicate. Census the whole predicate (each precondition's pass/fail, not just the verdict) and report which one binds. Here that turned "1,465 clusters affected" into "0 decisions change, and here is the single near-miss and why it still fails" — which is the difference between shipping a fix and shipping a fix WITH the evidence that it is safe. The change still ships: the gate is now correct by construction and A/B-neutral, which is the cheapest moment to fix a latent trap, not a reason to leave it.
- ⚠ **PENDING SKILL EDIT, fifth occurrence of #2376.** Writes to `.claude/skills/**` were DENIED again on this worktree. The `sec-edgar.md` §2.3 edit specified in the #2385 entry above is still unapplied; this session drafted it in full (four-writer table, the `GROUP BY 1,2` provenance query, the `source_document_id !~ ':(NDT|NDH):'` discriminator, and the rule that any read-path branch on `ownership_nature == 'direct'` must check `Holder.nature_from_table_i`) and could not write it. Apply on a session that has permission.
### An input-side exclusion rate is not an exposure rate when the consumer carries state (#2240 5e-5a, 2026-08-07)

- Symptom: criterion 9 asks for *"the count and share of bars/trades excluded per strategy"*, and on this corpus that census is reassuringly tiny — **643 of 23,339,583 bars flagged (0.002755%)**, on 370 of 5,266 series, measured over the full validated universe by `scripts/verify_2240_quarantine_sensitivity.py --census`. Read alone, that number says the quarantine cannot be moving anything. It says nothing of the sort.
- A masked field is not a one-bar hole; it is a hole the size of whatever reads it. For a rolling-window indicator the damage spans the window. For a **recursive** one it spans the rest of the series: `indicator_series.rsi_series` is Wilder-smoothed, so a NULL close *"poisons the recursion from that point on"* and every later index is marked unevaluable — which `app/services/strategies/s3_mean_reversion_in_trend.py`'s header already states, and which nothing in the census reflects. Measured on the FULL population (5,266 series, 23,339,583 bars): the **65** return-flagged closes produced **12,836** `quarantined_bar` verdicts in S-1 (197x) and **174,978** in S-3 (**2,692x**), all of which the admitted arm returns to zero. On three individual series, for the shape: 15 return-flagged closes on series 644 changed **854** S-1 signals and **5,540** S-3 ones; 9 on series 5707 changed **9,270** S-3 signals, the whole remainder of the series.
