- Enforced in: this prevention log; `frontend/src/lib/strategyFormat.ts` (sole definition of `number`/`money`/`pctPoints`); `frontend/src/components/strategies/StrategyPositions.tsx` docstring (records that the share rule binds the formatters, not just the components).

### Telemetry recorded after a fallible call in the same `finally` is lost exactly when it matters
- First seen in: #2855 PR #2873 (2026-08-23), caught by the review bot
- Symptom: `thesis_refresh` records `writer_loaded_s` — how long a 10 GB local model was held — in the batch loop's `finally`, so it survives an exception out of the loop. It was written as `release_local_models(clients)` *then* compute-and-record, in one `finally`. `release_local_models` is documented as never raising and today does not, so the code was correct; but the correctness rests on a promise in **another module's docstring**, and this ticket exists precisely because two such promises had gone stale silently. A release that started raising would send every failing run back to carrying no measurement — indistinguishable from a pre-instrumentation row, on the one question the instrumentation was added to answer.
- ⚠ The generalisation of the existing "each step in a multi-step `finally` gets its own `try`" entry, which is scoped to **shared-DB-schema restore**. The subject here is telemetry, the shape is identical, and the reason it reads as safe is different: nothing is *restored*, so the eye does not look for a partial-failure path.
- Prevention: when a value must survive a failure, record it in its own nested `try/finally` rather than after any other call in the same block — `try: <fallible cleanup> finally: <compute + record>`. Do not settle the question by reading the callee's docstring; the whole point of recording in a `finally` is that something upstream failed, and that is the state in which optimistic assumptions are least likely to hold. Test it by patching the cleanup to raise and asserting the value is still recorded (`tests/test_thesis_refresh_lock.py::test_load_window_survives_a_raising_release`) — an ordering test that passes under the wrong ordering is not one.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `app/workers/scheduler.py::thesis_refresh` (nested `finally`, with the reasoning at the call site); `tests/test_thesis_refresh_lock.py::test_load_window_survives_a_raising_release`.

### `.claude/**` writes fail from a linked worktree in TWO distinct classes — diagnosed, and neither is a filesystem problem (#2403, 2026-08-23)
- First seen in: #2403 (filed 2026-08-08 from `.ebull-ownership`); re-hit on #2838, #2840, #2834 step 0, #2834 ARM B step 1, and again here — the sixth occurrence, and the first on which the two refusals were told apart.
- Symptom: every `Edit`/`Write` under `.claude/**` is refused in a headless loop session, so the repo's own "Skill ownership" rule (*"fix the skill inline, in the same PR"*) is unenforceable. Lessons accumulate as drafted prose in this log instead of landing in the file anyone reads before starting work. Eight were parked when #2403 was filed.
- ⚠⚠ **There are two different refusals and they had been read as one.** They print differently and they have different fixes:

  | path | verbatim error | class |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `.claude/skills/quant/strategy-evidence.md` | `Claude requested permissions to write to <path>, but you haven't granted it yet.` | permission rule |
  | `.claude/skills/engineering/test-quality.md` | same | permission rule |
  | `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | `Claude requested permissions to edit <path> which is a sensitive file.` | harness-level, path-based |

- Measured this session, from `/Users/lukebradford/Dev/.ebull-autonomy` (a linked worktree):
  - The worktree's `.claude/settings.local.json` `permissions.allow` contains bare `Edit`, `Edit(//**)` **and** `Edit(~/.claude/**)`. **All three are insufficient** — the skills write is still refused. So `.claude/**` is not covered by a catch-all grant, and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s own claim that *"the `permissions.allow` block already grants Edit/Write on the whole tree — no per-skill approval prompt should appear"* is **false as written**.
  - `~/.claude/settings.json` grants twenty per-directory rules of the form `Edit(/.claude/skills/engineering/**)`. `engineering` **is** on that list and is **still refused** from this worktree — which kills the "the directory was simply never granted" theory (`quant` is indeed absent from the list, and adding it alone would not have helped).
  - There is **no** `PreToolUse` hook in any of the three settings scopes I can read; the only hooks are a `PostToolUse` Bash reminder and a `Stop` narrator. ⚠ That does not rule out a managed/enterprise or plugin policy I cannot observe from inside the session — it rules out the hooks *this repo* controls.
  - `~/.claude.json` has **no** project entry for this worktree at all, and `/Users/lukebradford/Dev/eBull`'s entry has `allowedTools: []`. The grants live only in the user-scope settings file.
  - `docs/` writes in the same session succeed with no prompt, so it is not the worktree, the filesystem, or the branch.
- ⚠ A shell `printf '' >> <file>` "writability test" reports **success** on both classes and detects neither — the refusal is in the Edit/Write tool layer. Test with a real one-character `Edit`, or assume refusal. (Third time this false-negative has been recorded.)
- Prevention, for the loop: when a lesson belongs in `.claude/skills/**`, **do not spend a turn discovering the refusal.** Write it here, and in the same entry name the exact target file and the anchor text it belongs beside, so applying it later is a mechanical edit rather than a re-derivation. State the occurrence count — a recurring per-case patch is the trigger to question the model, and six is well past it.
- ⚠⚠ **The two REFUSAL CLASSES are measured; the MECHANISM behind either is not.** "Permission rule" and "harness-level block" are labels inferred from two verbatim error strings, not from a controlled test. In particular, *"the six skill rules use a single leading slash and therefore anchor at the filesystem root"* is an **unsupported inference** — it is consistent with the observations and it is not the only thing that would produce them. Alternatives this session did **not** rule out: canonical-path / symlink resolution across a linked worktree; project-root or trust detection; settings precedence or a permission set cached at session start; `Edit`-vs-`Write` policy differing; an implicit sensitive-directory deny covering `.claude/**` wholesale; managed/enterprise policy outside the readable files; a plugin-supplied policy that is not a `PreToolUse` hook; or the session loading settings from the main checkout rather than this worktree. **Do not repeat the slash theory as established.**
- Prevention, for the fix: the candidate grant is one that matches the **absolute** path, e.g. `Edit(//**/.claude/skills/**)` — but the cleaner *mechanism test* is narrower: grant the exact canonical worktree path first (`Edit(//Users/lukebradford/Dev/.ebull-autonomy/.claude/skills/**)`) and see whether that alone lifts it. If it does, the cause is path resolution and a cross-checkout `//**` grant is broader than the evidence requires. Either way the grant is only a candidate **until re-tested after a session restart**, since a stale cached permission set is one of the live alternatives above.
- ⚠ **Why the loop did not apply it, stated exactly — this is an EXECUTION dependency, not a judgement I am deferring.** The repo bans labelling a derivable question "needs an explicit call", and this is not that: I have the recommendation and it is written above. The blocker is mechanical — `.claude/settings.local.json` is **itself under the refused path**, so a session cannot apply the grant, and could not verify it in-session even if it could write it (the set may be read once at start). The operator is needed to *execute and reload*, not to *decide*. ⚠ If a managed policy outside these files is what reserves permission-boundary changes to a human, that policy governs and repo prose cannot override it — which is another reason the narrow canonical-path test should be run before anyone widens anything.
- ⚠ `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is a **separate and harder** case: it refuses as a *sensitive file*, which is a harness-level protection on agent-instruction files rather than a missing grant. A permission widening aimed at `skills/**` should not be expected to unblock it, and a correction owed to `CLAUDE.md` needs a different route — an operator edit, or a pointer from a file that is writable.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; #2403 (diagnosis comment, 2026-08-23); `docs/proposals/ta/2026-08-23-sb-armb-verdict.md` §8 (records the same two-class finding beside the correction it blocks).

### "Beating buy-and-hold" is a narrative metric that reads as a verdict — s2's own numbers disagree with it in sign (#2834, 2026-08-23)
- First seen in: 2026-08-23, re-measuring #2834 ARM B step 1's §8 under working-order 3c before repeating its conclusion.
- Symptom: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/skills/quant/strategy-evidence.md` both carried *"s2 inside the turnover bar **and the only one beating buy-and-hold**"* — the standing reason a reader would treat s2's family as the promising one, and the premise ARM B inherited. #2834 falsified it and wrote the repair as *"negative on all five pinned hold-out views"*. **That repair is itself wrong on two counts.**
- Measured: pinning every key of `current_identity_pins()` (which fixes `namespace = 'hold_out'`, `benchmark_rule = 'equal_weight_buy_and_hold_v1'`, `return_basis = 'split-dividend-adjusted-wealth-v1'`) and counting **distinct `(window_start, window_end)`** returns **six** windows for s2, where #2834 reported five. ⚠ That #2834 *"omitted"* one is **not** established — it may have pinned a different namespace, a different revision, or counted rows rather than distinct windows. Safe statement: *#2834 reported five under a selection this pass did not reproduce, and the pinned selection returns six.* The extra window, `2022-01-01 → 2022-12-31`, is the only **positive** one: `return_vs_buy_and_hold_pct` `+13.35` (best_case) / `+9.59` (worst_case), against `−11.76 … −55.27` on the other five.
- ⚠⚠ The interesting half, and "losing less" is measured rather than inferred: on that window `total_return_pct` is **−12.07%** against a buy-and-hold of **−25.43%** — both negative, s2 merely less so — while `expectancy_per_trade_pct` is **−7.02% / −8.60%**. 2022 is the bear year and the whole `+13.35` is the benchmark falling further. **The decisive detail is `profit_factor`: 0.384 / 0.327 on that window, the WORST of all six** (0.286–0.660 elsewhere). The narrative metric is most flattering exactly where the decision metric is worst. s2's `total_return_pct` is negative on **all six** pinned windows; it never made money on any of them.
- ⚠ Not a contradiction, and saying so precisely matters: `return_vs_buy_and_hold_pct` is a **difference of two sleeve-level percentages** (`total_return - benchmark_return`, `app/services/strategy_statistics.py:530`) while `expectancy_per_trade_pct` is a **per-trade mean**; overlapping positions, idle cash and compounding stop either from reconstructing the other, so `+13.35` beside `−7.02` is arithmetically fine. The defect is not disagreement — it is that **only one of the two answers "is there edge here", and it is not the one that reads like a verdict.** Same structural objection for which `.claude/skills/quant/cost-aware-viability.md` already bans CAGR and Sortino.
- ⚠ **The code was already right and that is the point.** `return_vs_buy_and_hold_pct` is gated on nowhere — `app/services/synthetic_control_run.py:689` records it as a number *"which NEITHER of §9's two cuts consumes"*, and no promotion path reads it. The damage was done entirely in **prose**, in the two files a session reads before proposing a strategy. A metric can be correctly excluded from every gate and still steer the whole programme, because what selects the next ticket is a sentence, not a threshold.
- Prevention: `return_vs_buy_and_hold_pct` stays report-only — do not let it acquire a threshold. In prose it may answer the narrow question it actually measures (*"did the sleeve outperform this benchmark over this window?"*), and it may **not** stand in for *"does this strategy have edge?"* without `expectancy_per_trade_pct` and `profit_factor` beside it. That substitution is the whole defect here. When a skill sentence ranks strategies, it must name the metric it ranked on. And when correcting a quantified claim, **do not replace it with a second unmeasured quantifier** — "all five" was asserted from a table that had already dropped a row. This log's own rule binds the repair as much as the original: a sentence containing "every"/"all" about source data is a measurement, so run it or drop the word.
- ⚠ The skill edit is BLOCKED — see the `.claude/**` two-class entry above. Target: `.claude/skills/quant/strategy-evidence.md`, the paragraph beginning *"That stored snapshot had S-2 as the only one of the three above buy-and-hold"* (§1, immediately under the four-filter table), plus the same clause in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s `strategy-evidence.md` bullet. Full replacement text: `docs/proposals/ta/2026-08-23-sb-armb-verdict.md` §8, "Correction to apply".
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `docs/proposals/ta/2026-08-23-sb-armb-verdict.md` §8.1 (the six-window table + the sign-disagreement finding).

### A fail-closed predicate is not automatically safe on a DISPLAY surface — the same `!== true` that protects a decision path invents a defect on a list (#2306, 2026-08-23)
- First seen in: #2306, mirroring `thesis_subject_identity.is_thesis_usable` into the frontend so the screen would stop rendering theses the engine had already refused. Caught at Codex ckpt-1, before any code was written.
- Symptom: the backend predicate is `row.get("subject_identity_ok") is True`, deliberately treating NULL as *nobody decided* rather than *passed* — correct, and the reason `portfolio.py` stopped firing EXITs on wrong-company valuation bands. Copying it verbatim to the theses library would have marked **every held instrument that has no thesis at all** as "quarantined": `ThesisLibraryItem` gives those rows a place by design (`app/api/theses.py:235-239`, so the dashboard's staleness alert and the library it links to agree), with every thesis field NULL. `ok !== true` is true there for the trivial reason that there is nothing to check.
- ⚠⚠ **The asymmetry is the lesson, and it is not obvious in either direction.** On a decision path, "undecided" and "failed" are correctly collapsed: both mean *do not act on this*, so failing closed loses nothing. On a display surface they are different claims about the world — "this memo was checked and it failed" versus "there is no memo" — and collapsing them **manufactures a defect on a healthy row**, which is the failure mode that trains an operator to ignore the marker. Fail-closed is a property of the ACTION, not of the predicate; a surface that acts on nothing inherits none of its safety and all of its bluntness.
- ⚠ The tell is cheap to check and was already in the codebase: the row's own `thesis_id` is nullable, and the **critic cell two columns over already gated on `row.thesis_id !== null`**. A neighbouring cell rendering the same row's data under a different guard is the signal that the row has a "nothing here" state the new guard has not considered.
- ⚠ Second, related slip on the same ticket, also caught at ckpt-1: the state enum's `false` member was named `misattributed`, when the stored rule records only that the memo did not NAME its subject — a strictly weaker claim than "is about another company" (1,512 rows vs the ~19 of the narrower class). **A state name is a claim, and a wrong one propagates further than a wrong comment, because every later reader inherits it from the type.** Renamed `unnamed_subject`.
- Prevention: when mirroring a backend fail-closed predicate onto a read surface, enumerate the states the surface can be in that the DECISION path never sees — chiefly "the entity does not exist yet" — and gate on the existence key (`thesis_id`, `position_id`, …) *in addition to* the verdict. Pin the empty case by test explicitly, not just the pass and fail cases: `frontend/src/pages/ThesesPage.test.tsx::"does NOT mark a HELD row that has no thesis at all"` is the assertion that fails if the bare predicate comes back. Same rule as this log's existing NARROWING-gate entry, in the other direction: there, enumerate what a gate REJECTS; here, enumerate what a marker CLAIMS.
- ⚠ Where the lesson belongs but could not be written: `.claude/skills/frontend/safety-state-ui.md`, beside its "What counts as a safety-state indicator" section — that skill covers a safety indicator wrongly DISAPPEARING and has nothing on one wrongly APPEARING. Blocked by the two-class `.claude/**` refusal recorded above; apply it there when that is lifted.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `frontend/src/lib/thesisQuarantine.ts` (`isThesisQuarantined` docstring carries the "NOT SUFFICIENT ALONE ON A LIST SURFACE" warning at the definition); `frontend/src/pages/ThesesPage.tsx` (the gate, with the reason at the call site); `frontend/src/pages/ThesesPage.test.tsx`.

### A prettifying FALLBACK disguises a missing label as a written one — the gap becomes invisible to the only person who would report it (#2844, 2026-08-23)
- First seen in: #2844, wiring the capital-sandbox refusal onto /strategies. The acceptance clause is *"Guard refuses over-bound entries; refusal visible on /strategies"*, and the refusal WAS reaching the screen, which is why it read as done.
- Symptom: `StrategiesPage.tsx::refusalLabel` ended `?? refusal.replaceAll("_", " ")`. `strategy_paper_executor` can write **76** distinct `reason_code` values into `strategy_funding_decisions.reason_code`, and `REFUSAL_LABELS` described **3** of them — its other 37 entries are the *allocation-readiness* vocabulary, near-disjoint from the *paper-entry-preflight* one. So 73 codes, `sandbox_exceeded` among them, rendered as "sandbox exceeded": same slot, same styling, same register as the sentences someone actually wrote.
- ⚠⚠ **The transform is the defect, not the mitigation.** A raw identifier on screen is a visible gap and gets reported. A *de-underscored* identifier is typographically indistinguishable from authored copy, so it is invisible to the operator, to the reviewer, and to the screenshot in the QA pass. This is #2306's "a state name is a claim" one layer down: the disguise makes the product appear to assert something it never wrote. **Never prettify an unknown key in a display fallback — return it verbatim.** The ugliness is the signal, and it is the whole value of the fallback.
- ⚠ Both `strategy_funding_decisions` and `strategy_entry_preflights` are EMPTY on dev (`count(*) = 0`), so this path had never once rendered a real refusal. **A display surface with no rows is not covered by any check we run** — not the smoke test, not FE-QA, not the review bot. Its correctness has to be reasoned from the emitting vocabulary, because there is nothing to look at.
- ⚠ Same fallback was also carrying a CATEGORY error it concealed: `latest_operation_trigger` (`operator_close`, `strategy_exit` — normal outcomes, not refusals) was rendered through the refusal map and only read sensibly because of the prettifier. Removing the disguise surfaced it as a failing test. **When one renderer serves several vocabularies, the fallback is what lets them stay merged.**
- ⚠⚠ Secondary, and it cost four attempts: **an extractor that SHAPE-MATCHES under-reports silently.** Hand extractions of this vocabulary returned 32, then 77, then 83, then 84 — each matched a set of AST shapes and each missed a different one (`return None, "<code>", False`; the `(predicate, code)` table; `reason_code=reason or "<code>"`; bare `return SANDBOX_EXCEEDED`). A guard built on any of them would have certified full coverage of the codes it happened to see. **Fix: within each position that matters, walk the WHOLE sub-expression rather than matching a shape, and pin one anchor per known shape so a stopped-recognising extractor fails loudly.** Over-inclusive is the correct error direction — a false positive costs one label, a false negative ships an unreadable code.
- ⚠ This guard is keyed on the refusal CODE, which this log's #2625 entry warns against. That entry's own general test is why it does not transfer: there the codes were a many-to-many projection of the gate INPUTS being constrained, so the assertion was identical with the defect present. Here the code string IS the thing displayed, so it is the index, not the observable. **The rule is "key on the artefact the feared edit necessarily produces" — not "never key on codes".**
- ⚠ Where a vocabulary IS declared, key on the declaration instead of a scrape: position-operation triggers are enumerated by `strategy_position_operations_trigger_code_check` (sql/292), so their guard parses the CHECK and asserts BOTH inclusion directions rather than restating the six values.
- Prevention: any `Record<string, string>` mapping engine codes to operator copy needs (a) a verbatim fallback, and (b) a test that the emitting vocabulary is covered. When the vocabulary is schema-declared, read the constraint; when it is only implicit in the emitting module — as this one is, and that is itself the underlying defect — walk the AST over-inclusively and self-test the walker.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `frontend/src/pages/StrategiesPage.tsx` (`REFUSAL_LABELS` header states the two vocabularies; the `refusalLabel` comment states why an unknown code is returned verbatim; `TRIGGER_LABELS` split out with its source constraint named); `tests/test_2844_refusal_labels_cover_executor.py` (five tests — coverage, extractor self-test, trigger-vs-CHECK both directions, allow-list minimality, and a no-restated-identifiers check; all revert-probed).
### A spectacular return can be synthetic exchange traffic — classify the instrument before filtering the number
- First seen in: #2912 (2026-08-23), exposed by the preregistered French/AQR factor validation.
- Symptom: the full-population S-2 diagnostic correlated only `+0.026861` with French MOM and `+0.023260` with AQR, driven by a `-25.113837` March 2019 factor month. The bottom leg contained `ZBZZT`, whose stored close changed `14 → 199999.99`; Nasdaq's own alert and Symbol Directory identify it as a test security, not a company. Price quarantine admitted the move because synthetic volume corroborated it.
- Prevention: investigate an extreme member ledger by instrument identity before adding any magnitude rule. For U.S. equities, use the official Nasdaq Symbol Directory `Test Issue=Y` field, freeze the source hashes/set for a pinned corpus, exclude before alive/terminated classification, count the bucket so the vendor census still reconciles, and move the universe-rule identity. Never solve this class with winsorisation, a `Z*` prefix rule, or a post-result return cap.
- Reproduce: `PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m scripts.report_2912_factor_validation`; the invalid and corrected results plus both preregistration hashes are retained in `docs/proposals/ta/2026-08-23-r6-factor-validation-result.md`.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `.claude/skills/data-sources/research-price-corpus.md` §"Exchange test issues are not outliers"; `app/services/universe_selection.py::EXCHANGE_TEST_ISSUE_SYMBOLS`; `tests/test_2721_universe_selection.py`.

### A historical freeze script must not import a moving current strategy identity
- First seen in: #2912 (2026-08-23), when the exchange-test correction deliberately moved the hashed universe rule and therefore every manifest strategy version.
- Symptom: `freeze_2840_sh_regime_gate_declaration.py` recomputed S-11's version from the current manifest, while its immutable trial-register entry still claimed the original version. The pure gate failed before push; changing the trial would have falsely transferred already-seen evidence onto a different population.
- Prevention: a script for an already-registered historical declaration reads `(strategy_id, strategy_version)` from its immutable `DeclaredTrial`. Current-version derivation belongs only to a new declaration and new trial charge. When a shared input-rule hash moves, run the entire pure tier so old freeze scripts cannot silently relabel evidence.
- Enforced in: this prevention log; `scripts/freeze_2840_sh_regime_gate_declaration.py`; `tests/test_2840_sh_declaration.py`.
